name: Usage-based policy limits
blurb: Limits that scale with active GPU consumption and deployment footprint.
summary: Limits that scale with active GPU consumption and deployment footprint.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: A sublimit for bodily injury or property damage arising from artificial intelligence outputs that caps coverage at a fixed amount regardless of active GPU count.
An exclusion for failure to perform or contractual liability that removes coverage for service level agreement penalties triggered by usage spikes.
A business interruption waiting period that begins only after physical damage to the data centre, leaving no cover for cloud provider outages or denial of service attacks.
A property limit based on fixed square footage or maximum electrical capacity that does not increase when the insured adds GPU racks or liquid cooling systems.
A cyber sublimit that does not scale with usage, so a ransomware attack during a peak inference period exhausts the limit before business interruption losses accrue.
An exclusion for contingent business interruption from upstream utility or telecommunications failures, which are common during high GPU demand.
A definition of deployment footprint that excludes edge devices or third party hosted models, leaving gaps when the insured expands beyond its own data centres.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: A manuscript definition of active GPU consumption that uses a 30 day rolling average of GPU hours rather than instantaneous peak, to avoid limit exhaustion from short bursts.
An endorsement that locks the policy limit at the higher of the limit in force at the time of loss or the limit in force at the time the claim is first reported, preventing retroactive reduction.
A carve back that removes any sublimit for artificial intelligence outputs and instead treats model outputs as part of the general technology errors and omissions limit.

An audit clause that gives the insurer access to cloud provider billing records and orchestration logs but requires the insurer to bear the cost of any audit unless usage is underreported by more than ten percent.
A true up endorsement that adjusts premium annually based on actual usage but caps any additional premium at twenty five percent of the original premium to avoid surprise charges.
A manuscript exclusion removal for contingent business interruption from utility and telecommunications failures, with a sublimit that scales with the number of active GPU regions.
A definition of deployment footprint that includes edge devices and third party hosted models, with a separate sublimit for those exposures that also scales with usage.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: Business interruption waiting periods are typically 24 to 72 hours, but for usage based limits the waiting period may be reduced to 12 hours if the insured can demonstrate that a usage spike caused the loss.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Business interruption coverage is written on a gross earnings basis with a limit that scales with the insured's monthly recurring revenue from GPU compute, and includes an extended period of indemnity of at least 180 days to cover ramp up after a loss.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Electronic data processing equipment coverage is typically written on a blanket basis with a limit that scales with the total insured value of GPUs, servers, and networking gear, subject to a separate sublimit for transit and installation.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Property coverage is written with a per occurrence limit that scales with the replacement cost of active GPU racks and supporting electrical and cooling infrastructure, layered from a primary layer up to excess layers that attach based on the current deployment footprint.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: Primary commercial general liability is typically written on an occurrence basis with a per occurrence limit that scales from a base of one million dollars up to a multiple tied to peak active GPU count, subject to a minimum annual aggregate.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Claims made for the technology errors and omissions, cyber, and media liability portions because usage based limits require periodic reporting and retroactive adjustment, while occurrence based applies to sudden and accidental physical damage to third party property from data centre operations.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess liability towers are structured in layers that also scale with usage, with each layer attaching above the scaled primary limit and requiring monthly bordereaux of GPU hours to confirm attachment points.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Bodily injury or property damage to third parties arising from a fire, water leak, or power failure at a data centre where active GPU racks overheat.
Technology errors and omissions claims from customers who suffer financial loss when an AI model produces incorrect, biased, or harmful outputs.
Network security and privacy liability from a breach of the data centre's management plane that exposes customer data or allows unauthorized access to GPU clusters.
Intellectual property infringement claims alleging that training data or model weights used on the insured's GPUs violate third party copyrights or trade secrets.
Failure to supply or contractual liability when a usage spike causes the insured to breach service level agreements with cloud tenants or AI platform users.
Product liability for physical harm caused by an AI enabled device or robot whose inference runs on the insured's GPU infrastructure and malfunctions.
Pollution or environmental liability from coolant leaks or battery storage fires associated with high density GPU deployments.

underwriter_wants_to_know: How the insured measures active GPU consumption, whether by GPU hours, peak concurrent GPUs, or teraflops, and who certifies the telemetry.
What triggers a limit step up or step down, and whether the insured must notify the insurer before deploying additional GPUs or expanding to new regions.
Whether the usage metric is based on average daily active GPUs or peak instantaneous usage, because a burst of inference traffic could exhaust limits mid period.
How often the insured reports usage, and whether the insurer has audit rights over cloud provider billing records and orchestration logs.
What happens to outstanding claims if usage drops after a loss, and whether limits are locked at the time of loss or at policy inception.
Whether the deployment footprint includes edge devices, third party hosted models, or only the insured's own data centres, because each creates different aggregation risk.
How retroactive premium adjustments are calculated if actual usage exceeds the initial estimate, and whether there is a true up at expiry.
